safe_name: Jang Beom June - Your Shampoo Scent In The Flowers
song: Your Shampoo Scent In The Flowers

song_story.overview: This song is about the small, repetitive ritual of almost reaching out to someone and never quite doing it. The narrator keeps catching a hint of familiar shampoo scent among flowers and turns around expecting to see the person he misses, only to find strangers. He walks the same route home every day, fidgeting with his phone, working up the nerve to call, and talking himself out of it every single time. Nothing dramatic happens in the song — it's built entirely from the same small loop repeating: almost calling, not calling, walking home alone again.
song_story.cultural_root: The song's structure — the same walk, the same street, the same hesitation played out over and over — reflects a very grounded, everyday take on longing rather than a grand romantic gesture. 용기내 보지만 (I try to gather courage, but...) is a phrase pattern common in Korean songs about unspoken feelings, where the emphasis isn't on rejection but on never even getting to the point of being rejected, because the call never gets made.

verse_1.lines: 흔들리는 꽃들 속에서heundeullineun kkoccdeul sogeseo / 네 향풍향이 느껴져야ne syampuhyangi neukkyeojingeoya / 스쳐 지나간 건가 뒤돌아보지만seuchyeojinagangeonga dwidorabojiman / 그냥 사람들만 보이는 거야geunyang saramdeulman boineungeoya / 다와가는 집 근처에서dawaganeun jipgeuncheoeseo / 괜히 핸드폰만 만지는 거야gwaenhi haendeuponman manjineungeoya / 한 번 연락해 볼까 용기내 보지만hanbeon yeonrakhae bolkka yongginae bojiman / 그냥 내 마음만 아픈 거야geunyang nae maeumman aswiun geoya / 걷다가 보면 항상 이렇게 너를geotdaga bomyeon hangsang ireohge neoreul
verse_1.literal: Among the flowers swaying in the wind / I catch the scent of your shampoo / did you pass by just now? I turn around, but / it's just strangers I see / near the house I'm almost home to / I fidget with my phone for no reason / I try to gather the courage to call once, but / it's just my own heart that ends up hurting
verse_1.context: 그냥 내 마음만 아픈 거야 — 'it's just my own heart that ends up hurting' — 그냥 (just/simply) undercuts the moment, framing the pain as pointless and self-inflicted rather than meaningful, which fits the song's low-key, defeated tone.

chorus.lines: 바라만 보던 너를baraman bodeon neoreul / 기다린다고 말할까gidarindago malhalkka / 지금 집 앞에 계속 이렇게 너를jigeum jibape gyesok ireohge neoreul / 아쉬워 하다 너를 연락했었다 할까aswiwo hada neoreul yeonrakhaessda halkka / 진짜치는 꽃들 속에서jinachineun kkoccdeul sogeseo / 네 향풍향만 보이는 거야ne syampuhyangman boineungeoya / 스쳐 지나간 건가 뒤돌아보지만seuchyeojinagangeonga dwi dorabojiman / 그냥 내 마음만 바빠지는 거야geunyang nae maeumman bappajingeoya / 걷다가 보면 항상 이렇게 너를geotdaga bomyeon hangsang ireohge neoreul
chorus.literal: When I walk, I'm always like this, watching you / just watching you from afar / should I say I've been waiting? / right now, still like this, in front of your house / should I say I called because I missed you?
chorus.context: 바라만 보던 — '[the you] I could only watch' — 만 (only) narrows the verb down to its most passive form; he's not interacting with her at all, only observing, and the whole chorus is a list of things he considers saying but is only rehearsing, never actually delivering.

verse_2.lines: 바라만 보던 너를baraman bodeon neoreul / 기다린다고 말할까gidarindago malhalkka / 지금 집 앞에 계속 이렇게 너를jigeum jibape gyesok ireohge neoreul / 아쉬워 하다 너를 연락했었다 할까aswiwo hada neoreul yeonrakhaessda halkka / 어떤 계절이 너를eotteon gyejeori neoreul / 우연히라도 너를 마주치게 할까uyeonhirado neoreul majuchige halkka / 난 이대로 아쉬워하다nan idaero aswiwohada / 너를 바라만 보던 너를neoreul baraman bodeon neoreul / 기다리면서 아무말 못하고gidarimyeonseo amumal moshago
verse_2.literal: Among the flowers now in bloom / I can only see your shampoo scent / did you pass by just now? I turn around, but / it's just my heart getting busier, that's all
verse_2.context: 네 향풍향만 보이는 거야 — literally 'only your shampoo scent is what's visible' — a slight synesthetic slip, treating a smell as something 'seen,' which suggests the memory is so persistent it overrides his other senses.

final_line.lines: 그리워만 할까geuriwoman halkka / 걷다가 보면 항상 이렇게 너를geotdaga bomyeon hangsang ireohge neoreul / 바라만 보던 너를baraman bodeon neoreul / 생각한다고 말할까saenggakhandago malhalkka / 지금 집 앞에 기다리고jigeum jibape gidarigo / 때론 지나치고 다시 기다리는ttaeron jinachigo dasi gidarineun / 꽃이 피는 거리 보길 바라 이 밤에kkocci pineun georie bogopara ibame / 걷다가 보면 항상 이렇게 너를geotdaga bomyeon hangsang ireohge neoreul / 아쉬워 하다 너를aswiwo hada neoreul / 기다린다고 말할까gidarindago malhalkka / 지금 집 앞에 계속 이렇게 너를jigeum jibape gyesok ireohge neoreul / 아쉬워 하다 너를 연락했었다 할까aswiwo hada neoreul yeonrakhaessda halkka
final_line.literal: I hope some season brings you to me / even by coincidence, to run into you / I stay like this, missing you / just watching you, the you I only ever watched / waiting without being able to say anything / will I just end up missing you instead?
final_line.context: 우연히라도 (uyeonhirado) — 'even if by coincidence' — he's given up on making anything happen deliberately and is left hoping only for an accident to force the encounter he can't create himself.

artist_context: Jang Beom June is known for stripped-down, acoustic-leaning songwriting that favors small, specific, almost mundane details over sweeping romantic language, and this song is a clear example of that style — an entire song built around a scent and a walk home rather than any grand event.
honorific_level: informal — casual 반말, in a private, muttering-to-himself tone

grammar_highlights.usage: 'I try to do X, but...' Appears in 용기내 보지만 — 'I try to gather courage, but [fail].' Marks repeated, failed attempts.
Past-retrospective modifier for an ongoing past state. Appears in 바라만 보던 너를 — 'you, whom I only ever watched.'
Self-directed wondering question, 'should I...?' Repeated throughout the chorus (말할까, 할까) as a list of things he considers saying but doesn't.
